meta.parties: Kumarappa Chettiar, Et Al. v. Gunawathie Et Al

rules.statement: A mortgagee who has sued upon his bond and obtained a decree, but finds that the decree is of no avail against a puisne encumbrancer, can bring more than one action to enforce all or any of his remedies under a mortgage bond.
rules.supporting_quote: It has been urged that the principle underlying these two cases would be applicable or in any event could be extended so as to include the present case. There is a vital distinction between those cases and the one before me now. Those were cases of voluntary novation and the principle underlying was that where the novation was not real but merely nominal no novation could be said in fact to have taken place and the rights under the bond revived, or more properly, the bond was never novated. Here there has been a compulsory novation and it is sought to have the bond revived as against a stranger to it. The decree must first be got out of the way before the claim to have the bond considered revived can be entertained.
